b.x: The device lies. The ground does not

The battery dies. The screen wets. The cloud goes. The app points at a street that is closed. Whoever only follows the blue arrow stops when it stops. Navigation without GPS is not romance. It is the craft of knowing where you are, where you are going, and what to do when the bearing is wrong.
GPS gives a position. It does not give judgement. The chart and the eye give the rest.
A paper map does not ask for a network. A compass does not ask for an account.
Gray downloads the map at home. Rehearse the park on Sunday. In the field, the finger already knows.
CAUTION
The phone is backup. It does not replace a chart, a compass, a watch and the note at home. Field 10 (navigation) and Field apps: the digital downloads first. This field is the analogue.
STOP — before you walk farther
You lost the bearing: do not run. Whoever runs spends water and deepens the error. The public order, the same as civilian SERE: Sit. Think. Observe. Plan. Then walk — or stay and signal.
01 Sit. Water. Shade. One minute. The body stops lying.
02 Think. What was the last sure point? Hour. Direction of the sun. Sound of a river or a road.
03 Observe. Hill, valley, a line of light, a tower; moss is not enough. What the chart shows if you have it.
04 Plan. Back on your own track, go to a handrail (river, trail, fence), or stay and three whistles. One plan. Not three.
DON'T
Do not walk the bush at night to ‘find the way out’. Night erases the ground. Shelter, a signal, wait for light.
The chart in the hand

A 1:50,000 chart or the tourist map of the range. In the city, a street map with river and rail. Two: one at home, one in the pack, dry. Mark in pencil: home, point B, hospital, the drill trail. Plastic or a bag. Rain eats paper.
Orient the chart: chart north with compass north. The ground in front of you matches the drawing.
Finger on the place. The thumb does not leave the point. You walk, the thumb walks.
Scale: 1:50,000 → 1 cm is 500 m. 2 cm on the chart are a kilometre on the ground.
Contour lines tight = a slope. Spread = flat. Water goes down. So do you, if you choose the valley.
DO
Before you leave: three points on the chart you have already seen with your eyes. A drill. Without this the chart is a drawing.
The needle

A cheap baseplate compass will do. Away from the phone, a knife, a speaker, an electric fence. Hold it in the palm, at navel height, let the needle stop. The red end (on most) seeks magnetic north — which is not chart north.
01 On the chart: a line from the place to the destination. The compass base on the line.
02 Turn the bezel until its lines match chart north. Read the degree on the index.
03 Declination: in Brazil the value changes with place and year. The chart has the number. With no number, use the ground to correct — do not invent it.
04 On the ground: turn the body until the needle sits in the red house. Walk the direction-of-travel arrow. Not the needle.
05 A catch: a point ahead (tree, rock, tower). Walk to it. Take the bearing again. That way you do not zigzag.
NOTE
Three bearings to three known points cross where you are. Two already help. Rehearse in the park with the park’s chart.
Sun in Brazil — north is in the midday sky

In the southern hemisphere the sun at true midday is to the north. The shortest shadow points south. This reverses what the American film teaches. Whoever applies the northern trick here misses the whole bearing.
01 Shadow-stick: plant a straight stick. Mark the tip of the shadow. Wait 15 to 20 minutes. Mark again.
02 The line from the first mark to the second is west → east (the sun walks west; the shadow walks east).
03 The perpendicular is north–south. At midday in Brazil, the short shadow points south.

Analogue watch in the south: point the 12 at the sun. Halfway between 12 and the hour hand is north. Daylight-saving and a digital watch get in the way. The stick lies less. Rising sun is rough east; setting, rough west. Never millimetric. It is enough not to leave inverted.
DON'T
Moss, an anthill and ‘the church faces east’ are not a compass. They lie enough to lose the day.
The Southern Cross, not Polaris
Polaris does not show in Brazil. Whoever looks for the north star in the range’s sky will not find it. The Southern Cross will, most of the year, in a clear sky.
01 Find the four stars of the cross. The long arm runs from Gacrux (head) to Acrux (foot).
02 Extend the long arm beyond the foot, about four and a half times that arm’s length.
03 That point is near the south celestial pole. Drop plumb to the horizon: south.
NOTE
Moon and cloud erase the trick. The compass does not. That is why it goes in the pack even when the sky is clear on the drill.
DO
The whole sky — Cross, pointers, the false cross, Orion, the motion — is in the field Star orientation.
Read the ground
The chart without the eye is paper. The eye without the chart is a guess. Join the two. The ground has handrails, nets and stops — simple names so you do not get lost.
Handrail: a line you follow — river, trail, fence, road, ridge. Walk with it on the left or the right. Do not cross it by accident.
A collecting feature: a large point before the destination (clearing, bridge, a trail junction). You reach it, then take the fine bearing.
A catching feature: what sits AFTER the destination (a big river, a road, a hill). If you hit it, you overshot. Turn and come back.
Aiming off: point a little left of a confluence. When you hit the river, you know the destination is to the right. You do not guess both sides.
DO
Water goes down. In the Brazilian bush, following a river down often finds people, a road, a village. Up-river finds a spring and, sometimes, nothing. Choose with the chart, not with fear.
Pace and time

The metre is not in the pocket. The pace is. Rehearse a known hundred metres (a block, a pitch). Count each time the left foot hits the ground — the double-pace. Write the number. On a hill and with a load, the number rises. Recalibrate.
Flat, no load, an adult: about 60 to 70 double-paces per 100 m. Your number is the one that counts.
Time: 70–80 m a minute on the flat. Three kilometres ~40 minutes. A child, heat, the range: double it.
Mark every 100 m in the head or the notebook. You hit the catch too soon: the pace shrank. Too late: it stretched or the bearing was wrong.
The city with no blue arrow
Rivers, rails, valley avenues and hills are the city’s handrails. Name three axes of your city. Rehearse the walk to point B with no app.
Sun on façades: in Brazil, the north face takes more sun. Roughly useful. Not for crossing a neighbourhood.
Street numbers: even on one side, odd on the other. They grow in one direction. The corner plate is a chart.
A dish in Brazil often looks north (a satellite at the equator). A guess. Confirm with the sun.
Point A home, B family outside the neighbourhood, C a known public place. You split: do not wander. Go to the point.
Bush, range, coast

Amazonia, Cerrado, Atlantic forest, Caatinga, Pampa, the coast: GPS dies faster than water. Damp eats the battery. The trail dies in rain. The craft is the same: a chart of the region, not only the trail; a handrail; a catch; STOP.
Mark the way in (discreet house tape, a stone arrange you undo on the way back). Do not vandalise. Do not paint a tree.
A shortcut in the bush is rarely a shortcut. Back on the track if the ground worsens.
Coast: the sea is the handrail. The beach line does not lie. Entering the rock without the tide in the head is the classic error.
The range: a ridge is a handrail and also wind. A valley is water and also cold. Choose with the chart and the hour.
CAUTION

Lost: three whistles, three lights, a bright cloth. Emergency with last hour and clothes if there is a signal. Whoever stayed in camp is the anchor. Do not spread the group after one. Camp field and jungle field.
The minimum that walks
A chart of the region, dry, marked in pencil.
A baseplate compass. Away from the phone in the pack.
A watch. A pencil. A notebook. A whistle.
The phone with an offline map is the fourth item — not the first.
NOTE
Educational. It does not replace an orienteering course, a local guide or the authorities. Rehearse on the easy. Sunday in the park is worth more than the PDF.
DO
Reading the sheet — contours, scale, colours, the collar — is in the field Reading topographic maps.
